title: Lossless Asset Archiving for Digital Archives
business: Digital heritage organizations and archival libraries
problem: Lossy compression formats degrade historical image data over repeated save cycles, leading to permanent loss of detail in scanned documents.
solution: Utilizing the PNG format ensures lossless storage, where filtering and compression preserve all information, allowing for bit-for-bit reconstruction of the original scanned reference image.
steps: Convert raw high-resolution scans into the PNG reference image format.
Apply appropriate color space metadata using iCCP or sRGB chunks to ensure color fidelity.
Verify file integrity using the built-in Cyclic Redundancy Code (CRC) to detect transmission or storage corruption.
Store the resulting PNG datastream in the archival repository.
outcome: Historical documents are preserved with exact pixel-level accuracy, ensuring that future restorations or digital displays remain faithful to the original source.
limitation: PNG files are generally larger than lossy alternatives like JPEG, which can increase storage costs; check file size metrics against storage capacity limits.
